sections.h2: Picking up your car at Heathrow
sections.html: Heathrow has four passenger terminals (2, 3, 4 and 5). Most rental companies run their Heathrow branches from depots just outside the airport, reached by a short courtesy shuttle from the terminals. Follow the car rental signs in arrivals and check your voucher for the exact pick-up point and shuttle stop.

The airport sits right by the M4 and M25, so it’s quick to head west towards Windsor, Oxford, Bath and Cornwall, or around London on the M25. Remember the UK drives on the left. Heathrow is inside London’s Ultra Low Emission Zone (ULEZ); most modern rental cars meet the standard, but check with the rental company. Driving into central London also means the daily Congestion Charge, which the driver pays, so many visitors leave the car outside the centre.

• Allow time for the shuttle on the way back, as well as for refuelling near the airport.
  • Automatic cars are less common in the UK than in the US. Book early if you need one.
  • Check whether your rate includes the ULEZ-compliant car and any toll or charge admin fees.

faqs.q: Which terminal do I collect my Heathrow hire car from?
faqs.a: Most companies collect you from the terminal by shuttle and you pick the car up at their depot nearby. Your booking confirmation gives the meeting point for your terminal.

faqs.q: Do I pay the Congestion Charge in a rental car?
faqs.a: Yes, if you drive into the central London charging zone during charging hours, the driver is responsible for paying it. Unpaid charges are usually passed on by the rental company with an admin fee.
